title: A new Joomla site is born on the signed access verifier (0.2.0), not the header-trusting plg_system_tracyaccess 0.1.4 the Claude Cowork package installs, with no rollout.list line
steps: S1: Run provision/strict-site-access.sh on a site laid out as provision leaves it after the post-up hook (key + ready record, the Cowork package's 0.1.4 plugin, no rollout.list line).
S2: Run the Joomla and WordPress resync tools on a born-strict site and an unmarked neighbour.
S3: Run deploy-host-dsh.sh against a fake docker and read which resyncs it ran.
expect: S1: the plugin files equal provision/access/joomla/plg_system_tracyaccess (version 0.2.0), strict.json is written, an unproven site or a WordPress mu-plugin that is not the signed one fails the step, and provision runs the step after platform_post_up and before the baseline.
S2: the born-strict site is upgraded, the unmarked neighbour is held.
S3: the Joomla resync runs once after the WordPress one, and its failure fails the deploy.
evidence: Fresh local stand 27/10/2026: a new Joomla site ran plg_system_tracyaccess 0.1.4 from pkg_claudecowork 0.24.65, which trusts bare X-Tracy-Email/Tier/Role headers
fence: provision step 6c½, the born-strict marker in both resync tools, the deploy-time Joomla resync

tests: Joomla: the plugin the Cowork package installed is replaced by the signed verifier
the site is marked born strict
a site whose readiness was never proven fails the step
WordPress: the mu-plugin stage 6b copied is checked to be the signed one
provision runs the step after the post-up hook
a site born strict is resynced without a rollout.list line
the Joomla access plugin is resynced too
the Joomla resync fails: the deploy says so
